interaction_type.value: obstruction of dislocation glide by κ-carbides (glide plane softening)

qualitative_or_quantitative_description.value: Nano-scale κ-carbides obstruct dislocation glide; the glide plane softening effect of nano κ-carbides yields a lower strain hardening rate of the as-cast Cr-free strip. Reduced κ-carbide precipitation in Cr-containing strips results in a high strain hardening rate.

source.reason: Discussion states κ-carbides obstruct dislocation glide and their glide plane softening yields a lower strain hardening rate in the as-cast Cr-free strip.

interface_notes.value: FA (ferrite-to-austenite) solidification mode applies: L → L+δ → L+δ+γ → δ+γ; all ferrites are located in the centre of austenite grains, indicating δ-ferrite first nucleated and grew from the melt during near-rapid solidification.

source.reason: DF image using (010)κ shows κ-carbides located at the austenite/ferrite phase boundary, evidencing the γ/δ interface in the 0Cr strip.

slip_behavior.value: Slip bands in austenite are observed during deformation of the strips. In the as-cast 0Cr strip the average spacing between slip bands is ~90 nm and the average width of slip bands is 13.4 nm after tensile fracture. The slip spacing is relatively wide in the 0Cr strip due to localization of shearing caused by the higher obstruction of larger κ-carbides to dislocations.

source.reason: Slip-band spacing/width data for the as-cast 0Cr strip after tensile fracture, the dislocation-glide obstruction by κ-carbides, and the FA solidification sequence reported for this alloy.

comparison_metric.value: Effect of Cr addition on as-cast strip properties: Cr addition nonlinearly changes yield strength (first reduces to 617 MPa at 3Cr then increases to 740 MPa at 9Cr, both relative to the 724 MPa of Cr-free 0Cr) and clearly decreases total elongation of as-cast strips; it increases ultimate tensile strength and strain hardening rate.

source.reason: The 0Cr strip serves as the Cr-free reference for evaluating Cr addition effects on as-cast strips (yield strength evolution and decrease of total elongation).

method.value: centrifugal casting under near-rapid solidification condition — liquid metal poured into a copper mold at 600 r/min

processing_steps_notes.value: Alloy ingot made from high purity Fe (99.99%), Mn (99.9%), Al (99.9%), C (99.8%), Cr (99.9%); reheated to melt by an induction coil; liquid metal poured into a copper mold rotating at 600 r/min in Ar atmosphere; obtained strip size (60–80) mm × 60 mm × 2.5 mm. This as-cast strip is the un-annealed terminal condition and received no post-solidification heat treatment.

source.reason: This is the single production step for the as-cast 0Cr strip: the Fe–28Mn–9Al-1.2C-xCr ingot is re-melted and centrifugal-cast into a copper mold under near-rapid solidification; no heat treatment applies to the as-cast sample.

other_conditions.value: tensile tests by MTS Criterion Model 44 with 10 kN capacity; each test data supported by more than three tensile specimens; values averaged over 3 measurements

source.reason: Tensile test conditions for the strips: gauge size 20 mm × 4 mm × 1 mm at a strain rate of 1×10^-3 s^-1; values in Table 2 averaged over 3 measurements.
Table 2 (as-cast 0Cr strip) reports total elongation TE = 40.8 ± 8 %.

note.value: average strain hardening rate in the steady hardening stage (first of the four values 1626, 2048, 2266, 2385 MPa for 0Cr, 3Cr, 6Cr, 9Cr)

source.reason: Text gives the average strain hardening rates in the steady stage as 1626, 2048, 2266 and 2385 MPa for 0Cr, 3Cr, 6Cr and 9Cr respectively; 1626 MPa corresponds to the 0Cr strip.
Measured average density of the 0Cr strip is 6.49 g/cm3 (SJ-600G Electronic Water Displacement Density Analyzer).
Mechanical/physical property set for the as-cast 0Cr strip: tensile values from Table 2, strain hardening rate from the text, density from the experimental section.

dislocation_density.value: a few dislocations in austenite of 0Cr strip

source.reason: TEM of as-cast strips reports only a few dislocations in the austenite of the 0Cr strip (lowest dislocation content of the series).
XRD shows all strips are austenite + ferrite with austenite the major matrix phase; austenite lattice constant for the 0Cr strip is 3.70 Å.

distribution.value: clear superlattice present in austenite matrix of 0Cr strip; κ-carbides are only visible at the austenite/ferrite phase boundary in the DF image because sizes in the austenite are too small to identify

source.reason: SADP of the as-cast 0Cr austenite shows a clear κ-carbide superlattice; the average diameter of κ-carbides is 8 nm in the as-cast 0Cr strip and κ-carbides are only visible at the austenite/ferrite boundary.
The austenite matrix is the major phase of the as-cast 0Cr strip, containing a few dislocations and nano-scale κ-carbide precipitates with superlattice reflections.

Quantitative measurement by Gatan Digital Micrograph gives a ferrite fraction of 10.2 vol% for the 0Cr strip; Cr addition changes ferrite shape from rodlike to blocklike, so the 0Cr ferrite is rod-like.

region.value: dispersed uniformly in the austenite matrix (located at the centre of austenite grains)

source.reason: OM shows δ-ferrite dispersed in the austenite matrix; for the 0Cr strip ferrite amounts to 10.2 vol% and is rod-like.

number_of_phases.value: 2 (austenite γ + ferrite δ), plus κ-carbide precipitates

overall_structure.value: Two-phase microstructure composed of austenite (γ, major matrix phase) and ferrite (δ) uniformly distributed in the austenite matrix, together with nano-scale κ-carbide precipitates in the austenite; δ-ferrite first nucleated and grew from the melt according to the FA (ferrite-to-austenite) solidification mode.

source.reason: Overall phase assemblage and constituents of the as-cast 0Cr (Cr-free) strip.
